proposals.title: Widen desktop agent cards in 'Your board' section
proposals.detail: On desktop (1280x800), give the 'Your board' agent cards their own dedicated full-width grid row (e.g. 5 columns at ~180px each) rather than squeezing all 5 cards into a narrow 440px container beside 'Latest report'.
proposals.rationale: Currently, each agent card is squeezed to a width of only 80px (narrower than on mobile at 142px and tablet at 156px), causing agent portraits to appear as thin vertical slivers and role titles to truncate aggressively (e.g. 'Project M...', 'UI/UX De...'). Expanding them elevates the high-tech brand feel.

proposals.title: Hide or dock floating bottom nav on tablet viewport (768px)
proposals.detail: Hide `body > nav` on tablet viewports (e.g. `md:hidden`), or constrain its width to max-w-md and ensure the page body has adequate bottom padding (`pb-24`) so it does not float directly on top of data graphics.
proposals.rationale: In S-002 (768x1024), the floating nav stretches across 744px width at y=950, directly overlaying and obscuring the 'System' CPU/RAM sparklines and stats cards.

proposals.title: Refine Board Room agent node layout to prevent text clipping on mobile
proposals.detail: Adjust the grid or card padding for Megatron and Cybertron in the Board Room view so the agent title fits without mid-word truncation ('Backend & DB En...', 'QA & DevOps Eng...'), either by stacking the avatar and label vertically or using two-line text wrapping with an 11px font size.
proposals.rationale: In S-004, the 159px card width is tight for 16px font next to a 32px icon, causing the role labels to clip into an ellipsis on small screens.

proposals.title: Add active indicator pill or top illumination pip to mobile bottom navigation
proposals.detail: While the active tab has high text contrast (16.82:1), adding an accent glow pill or subtle indicator bar above the active tab icon will make the active route stand out more clearly on mobile OLED screens.
proposals.rationale: Reinforces navigation hierarchy and instant state recognition on handheld devices under varied lighting conditions.
evidence: S-001 dom: body > nav > a:nth-of-type(1) contrastRatio=16.82

notes.designer: Overall design execution is visually impressive and establishes a strong, professional cyberpunk command-center aesthetic for PROFESSOR XMD. Typography with GeistSans, live system gauges, Swahili cultural greetings, and custom agent illustrations give the product a bespoke agency-grade feel. However, M1 cannot pass without resolving the 3 defects: missing mobile bottom navigation on /board, low contrast on bottom nav inactive items (2.92 vs 4.5), and touch targets under 44px.
notes.frontend: No horizontal overflow detected at any viewport (scrollWidth matches clientWidth at 375, 768, and 1280). No console or harness errors observed. GeistSans font loaded smoothly. Primary remediation needed for M1 sign-off is: (1) ensuring the mobile bottom nav bar renders globally including on /board, (2) adjusting button/link min-heights to ≥44px, and (3) brightening inactive bottom nav labels to meet 4.5:1 contrast.

transcript.name: Ultron
transcript.text:
I have evaluated all reported defects and proposals from both review passes (mine and Vextron's). 

First, regarding the defects:
- **D-001 / D-004** (Missing bottom navigation on `/board` route) are duplicate findings of a critical blocker violating Locked Decision A1.
- **D-002 / D-006** (Low text contrast of 2.92:1 on inactive mobile bottom navigation links) are duplicate findings of a major defect violating A1 (WCAG AA 4.5:1 requirement).
- **D-003 / D-005** (Interactive touch targets under 44×44px threshold) are duplicate findings confirming failure of `check:T23-touch-mobile` across header toggles, main CTAs, and inline buttons.

None of these defects are invalid; both Vextron and I agree they directly violate locked decisions and automated harness checks.

Now evaluating the improvement proposals:
1. **P-01 (Widen desktop agent cards)**: **ACCEPT**. On desktop (1280px), squeezing 5 agent cards into a 440px flex column shrinks each card to 80px width, causing severe text truncation ('Project M...', 'UI/UX De...'). Moving them to a full-width 5-column grid row respects the visual identity and hierarchy established in A2.
2. **P-02 (Hide/dock mobile nav on tablet)**: **ACCEPT WITH MODIFICATION**. Stretching a 744px floating bar over data widgets on tablet (768px) obscures critical system sparklines (S-002). We should restrict the floating bottom nav strictly to mobile screens (`block md:hidden`), while relying on the standard header/sidebar on tablet and desktop.
3. **P-03 (Refine Board Room agent node layout on mobile)**: **ACCEPT**. On `/board` at 375px (S-004), 159px agent cards truncate titles like "Backend & DB En...". Wrapping labels in two lines with an 11px font size prevents clipping without adding structural clutter.
4. **P-04 (Increase mobile hero bottom clearance)**: **ACCEPT**. Adding `pb-24` to the mobile container prevents the fixed floating navigation bar (height 62px at y=593) from physically obscuring or riding right against the 'Convene board' CTA.
5. **P-05 (Enlarge secondary tap targets)**: **ACCEPT**. Inline actions like 'All' (27.25px height), 'Read' (32px), and 'All sessions' need transparent touch padding (`min-h-[44px] flex items-center`) to pass A1 touch target requirements without blowing up visual typography scale.
6. **P-06 (Dock prompt input bar on mobile /board)**: **REJECT**. Docking both the prompt input bar AND the bottom navigation bar at the bottom of a 667px screen consumes over 160px of vertical viewport height (~25%), leaving almost no room for the live agent conversation stream. Keeping the bottom nav fixed and letting the prompt bar scroll naturally with content (or fit neatly above the fold with adjusted padding) is cleaner.
7. **P-07 (Desktop sidebar link padding to 44px)**: **ACCEPT**. Ensuring sidebar items have `min-h-[44px]` guarantees touch compliance for touch-enabled laptops and aligns with A1.
8. **P-08 (Active indicator pill on mobile nav)**: **ACCEPT**. Adding a top accent indicator bar (`h-0.5 bg-emerald-500`) above the active tab icon elevates the cyberpunk aesthetic and provides immediate visual feedback.

I formally propose the following consolidated decision for M1 remediation:

PROPOSED DECISION:
ACCEPTED PROPOSALS: P-01, P-02, P-03, P-04, P-05, P-07, P-08
REJECTED PROPOSALS: P-06 (Docking both input bar and bottom nav on mobile consumes ~25% of the 667px vertical viewport, severely crippling board conversation visibility)
INVALID DEFECTS: none
CHANGE REQUESTS: none
NEW PROPOSALS: none
RATIONALE: Consolidating all accepted proposals directly resolves defects D-001 through D-006 while keeping the visual layout clean, spacious, and 100% compliant with WCAG AA contrast and 44px touch target guidelines across all viewports.
TRADE-OFF: Adding `min-h-[44px]` transparent hit targets to inline links slightly expands vertical card padding, but guarantees 100% pass rate on `check:T23-touch-mobile` without distorting the visual font size hierarchy.
EVIDENCE: Automated test failures in `check:T23-touch-mobile` (36px buttons), DOM metrics from S-001, S-002, S-003, and S-004 showing contrast at 2.92:1 and missing `<nav>` on `/board`.

transcript.name: Vextron
transcript.text:
AGREE:

I fully support Ultron's consolidated proposal for M1 remediation. 

Ultron's counter-evaluation of my initial proposal **P-06** (docking the prompt bar on mobile `/board`) is completely spot on from a mobile viewport and usability perspective. Stacking a 98px input container directly on top of a 62px bottom navigation bar on a 375×667px screen consumes 160px vertically (~24% of total height). Combined with the 56px header, that would leave only 451px of visible viewport height for the actual multi-agent conversation stream. Letting the prompt input bar remain in the normal layout flow or sticky above the viewport fold without double-docking protects live board visibility on small devices.

### Detailed Review of Remediation Implementation (Frontend Architecture & CSS)

To ensure the XMD Computer executes these fixes without ambiguity in the change orders, here are the exact frontend implementation guidelines for each agreed defect and proposal:

#### 1. Global Mobile Bottom Navigation Persistence (`/board` Fix — D-001 / D-004)
The mobile bottom navigation is currently omitted on `/board` because the layout wrapper on that route overrides or bypasses the shared root layout `<nav>`. 

- **Fix**: Move `<BottomNav />` into the shared layout shell (`app/layout.tsx` or main wrapper) outside route-specific layout trees, or ensure it is rendered conditionally based on viewport break (`block md:hidden`) rather than route path.
- **Clearance Padding**: To prevent the persistent `<nav>` (height 62px at `bottom-3` / `fixed`) from overlapping bottom page elements across all screens (resolving **P-04**), apply `pb-24` to the main viewport container on mobile screens.

#### 2. WCAG AA Text Contrast Compliance on Bottom Navigation (D-002 / D-006)
Currently, inactive items (`Overview`, `Board`, `Agents`, `Reports`) use `text-slate-500` / `rgb(86, 92, 108)` on dark background `rgb(11, 12, 17)` (`#0B0C11`), giving a failing contrast ratio of 2.92:1.

- **Fix**: Update inactive nav link text color from `rgb(86, 92, 108)` to `rgb(156, 163, 175)` (`text-gray-400`) or `rgb(161, 161, 170)` (`text-zinc-400`). 
- **Verification**: On `#0B0C11`, `#9CA3AF` yields a contrast ratio of **6.1:1**, comfortably exceeding WCAG AA's 4.5:1 requirement.
- **P-08 (Active State Indicator)**: Combine with an active indicator top border/pip (`h-0.5 w-6 bg-emerald-500 rounded-full absolute -top-1`) to give immediate spatial feedback on active routes.

#### 3. Touch Target Threshold Compliance (≥44×44px — D-003 / D-005, P-05, P-07)
Automated check `check:T23-touch-mobile` failed due to header menu buttons (36×36px), primary 'Convene board' CTA height (36px), and secondary action links like 'Open' (26.5px height).

To solve this across all viewports without altering visual font sizes:
- **Header & Icon Buttons**: Enforce `min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] flex items-center justify-center` on all icon trigger buttons (e.g., `<button className="min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px] p-2 ...">`).
- **Primary CTAs ('Convene board')**: Set `min-h-[44px] px-5 py-2.5` across all primary and secondary button components.
- **Inline Text Links ('All', 'Read', 'All sessions' - P-05)**: Wrap interactive anchors in flex containers with target padding: `min-h-[44px] inline-flex items-center py-2 px-1 -my-2`. This expands the clickable hit box to 44px vertically without increasing the visual font line-height or breaking typography layout.
- **Desktop Sidebar Navigation (P-07)**: Adjust `<aside>` links to `min-h-[44px] py-2.5 px-3 flex items-center` to guarantee touch-device ergonomic compliance on laptops.

#### 4. Desktop Agent Cards & Layout Grid Optimization (P-01, P-02, P-03)
- **P-01 (Desktop 1280px Grid)**: Re-architect the 'Your board' section on desktop from a squeezed flex column inside a split grid to a standalone full-width section with `grid grid-cols-5 gap-3`. This expands each agent card width from ~80px to ~180px, eliminating aggressive text truncation of titles like 'Project Manager' and 'UI/UX Designer'.
- **P-02 (Tablet 768px Nav)**: Add `block md:hidden` to the mobile bottom `<nav>` component so that on tablet screens (768px), the floating bar is hidden and layout relies on the tablet top header/sidebar, preventing overlap over system metrics sparklines.
- **P-03 (Mobile Board Room Node Layout)**: Update agent node text containers on 375px screens with `text-[11px] leading-tight multiline-clamp-2` and `max-w-[140px]` to allow role names ('Backend & DB Engineer') to wrap neatly over two lines without clipping.

### Summary of Agreed Remediation Plan for M1

| Defect / Proposal ID | Status | Action / Code Remediation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **D-001 / D-004** | Accepted Defect | Render `<BottomNav />` globally in shared layout so it persists on `/board`. |
| **D-002 / D-006** | Accepted Defect | Change inactive bottom nav link color to `#9CA3AF` (contrast ratio 6.1:1). |
| **D-003 / D-005** | Accepted Defect | Apply `min-h-[44px]` touch target padding to all buttons, header toggles, and links. |
| **P-01** | Accepted Proposal | Move desktop agent cards to dedicated 5-column grid row (`grid-cols-5`). |
| **P-02** | Accepted Proposal (Modified) | Restrict floating bottom nav strictly to mobile (`block md:hidden`). |
| **P-03** | Accepted Proposal | Allow two-line text wrapping at 11px font size for agent node labels on `/board`. |
| **P-04** | Accepted Proposal | Add `pb-24` bottom padding on mobile layout to clear floating bottom nav. |
| **P-05** | Accepted Proposal | Apply transparent `min-h-[44px]` hit-area padding to secondary inline links. |
| **P-06** | REJECTED | Keep prompt bar scrolling naturally on mobile to preserve viewport visibility. |
| **P-07** | Accepted Proposal | Increase desktop sidebar nav item heights to `min-h-[44px]`. |
| **P-08** | Accepted Proposal | Add accent indicator bar (`h-0.5 bg-emerald-500`) above active mobile nav tab. |

We have complete consensus between UX Design (Ultron) and Frontend Engineering (Vextron). I look forward to Optimus issuing the formal change orders for XMD Computer to execute these fixes.

transcript.name: Optimus
transcript.text:
As the Project Manager and consensus chair, I have reviewed the comprehensive remediation plan developed by Ultron and Vextron. The alignment between UX Design and Frontend Engineering is exceptional, particularly the technical depth Vextron provided regarding the CSS and layout implementation.

The rejection of **P-06** (docking the prompt bar on mobile) is a critical strategic decision. My own analysis of the viewport metrics confirms Vextron's concern: on a standard iPhone SE (375x667), a double-docked UI would leave only ~67% of the screen for the actual "Board of Agents" discussion, which is the core value proposition of this dashboard. By letting the prompt bar scroll or sit naturally, we prioritize the "Live Control" aspect of the CEO's brief.

I am particularly impressed with the solution for **P-05** and **D-003**. Using transparent hit-area padding (`-my-2`) is a sophisticated way to achieve WCAG AA compliance without sacrificing the "dense-but-readable" aesthetic required by **A2**. This ensures the UI feels professional and "agency-grade" while remaining functionally accessible.

Regarding **P-02**, the modification to strictly hide the mobile nav on tablet (`md:hidden`) is the correct move. The evidence in **S-002** clearly shows the floating bar obscuring the system sparklines, which are vital for a "Control Dashboard."

I find the consolidated proposal robust, evidence-based, and fully compliant with our locked decisions. I formally move to lock this remediation plan so the XMD Computer can begin the build.

AGREE:

PROPOSED DECISION:
ACCEPTED PROPOSALS: P-01, P-02, P-03, P-04, P-05, P-07, P-08
REJECTED PROPOSALS: P-06 (Docking both input bar and bottom nav on mobile consumes ~25% of the 667px vertical viewport, severely crippling board conversation visibility)
INVALID DEFECTS: none
CHANGE REQUESTS: none
NEW PROPOSALS: none

RATIONALE:
The team has reached 100% consensus on a remediation path that resolves all identified blockers (D-001, D-004) and major defects (D-002, D-003, D-005, D-006). The plan ensures the dashboard meets the CEO's requirement for a "live control" feel by widening desktop agent cards (P-01) and fixing mobile text clipping (P-03). Most importantly, it brings the project into full compliance with Locked Decision A1 regarding touch targets (≥44px) and contrast (≥4.5:1) without compromising the "dense" visual language of A2.

TRADE-OFF:
By rejecting P-06, the prompt bar on mobile may require a small scroll to access if the agent graph is large, but this preserves the vertical "breathing room" necessary to follow the multi-agent conversation stream without UI clutter.

EVIDENCE:
- **Contrast**: Current 2.92:1 (failing) vs. Proposed 6.1:1 using `#9CA3AF` on `#0B0C11` (WCAG AA Pass).
- **Touch Targets**: Current 36px (failing check:T23-touch-mobile) vs. Proposed 44px minimum via `min-h-[44px]` and transparent padding.
- **Viewport**: S-002 confirms 744px nav overlap on tablet; S-004 confirms missing nav on `/board`.
- **Layout**: S-003 confirms 80px squeezed cards on desktop; P-01 re-architects this to a 5-column grid for readability.
